newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canada's Placer Dome agrees to Highlands deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Placer Dome agrees to Highlands deal.

text.p: Canadian gold giant Placer Dome Inc. Tuesday agreed to a deal with Papua New Guinean miner Highlands Gold Ltd. that gives Placer control of the giant PNG Porgera gold mine and ends a bitter feud between the two miners.
The deal also keeps the Highlands group as a listed company free to develop base metal and gold projects in the resource rich Pacific island nation.
Under the complex plan, the Vancouver-based miner would pay Highlands A$316.1 million ($249.7 million) to buy Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera mine.
Placer had previously offered Highlands A$276.8 million ($218.7 million) for its Porgera stake after building up a 40-percent stake in Highlands through a hostile takeover bid.
"We am pleased that Placer has accepted our offer," Highlands managing director Ian Goddard said in a statement.
Highlands will spin off a new company, Highlands Pacific Ltd., which would hold the Ramu nickel/cobalt and Frieda-Nena copper/gold projects as well as its exploration porfolio in PNG and Indonesia.

Under the restructuring of the Highlands group about A$160 million ($126.4 million) would be raised through a mixture of new equity and the planned sale by Placer Dome of the shareholding it would inherit in Highlands Pacific.

Placer Dome already has effective control over the 25 percent stake in Porgera through its Australian offshoot Placer Pacific Ltd. The Canadian miner plans to buy out the remaining 24.6 percent stake in the Australian unit.
Placer Dome's orginal bid of 75 cents per Highlands share, which valued Highlands at A$423 million ($334 million), was launched on Nov. 28, 1996 and was rejected by Highlands.
